lessons.title: Correct Form of Personal Pronouns
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Use I, he, she, we, they as the subject of a sentence, and after "and" - "Naureen and I were present."
  • Use me, him, her, us, them as the object - "You are taller than him."
  • Use who for the subject - "It was Salma who called on you."
  • Use a possessive pronoun when nothing follows it - hers, ours, his - "These books are not hers."
  • Use a possessive adjective before a noun - her, our, his - "He lost his bat."

Solved Exercises

1. Naureen and ______ were present. (I, me)
I

2. It was Salma ______ called on you. (who, whom)
who

3. It might have been ______. (he, him)
he

4. You are taller than ______. (he, him)
him

5. He is a better batsman than ______. (we, us)
us

6. Is that Shilla? Yes, it is ______. (she, her)
her

7. Nobody but ______ was absent. (she, her)
she

8. She and ______ are good friends. (I, me)
I

9. Your pen writes better than ______. (her, hers)
hers

10. These books are not ______. (her, hers)
hers

11. He lost his bat and we ______. (our, ours)
ours

12. The bike which has been stolen is not ______. (his, him)
his

lessons.title: Correct Form of Adjectives
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Comparative: add -er or use more - "prettier", "more beautiful", "wiser".
  • Superlative: add -est or use most - "richest", "tallest", "most difficult".
  • Irregular forms: good - better - best and bad - worse - worst.
  • Use the comparative when two things are compared, and the superlative when one is compared with all the rest.

Solved Exercises

1. She is ______ than I. (pretty)
prettier

2. My father is ______ than Ali's father. (old)
older

3. My father is the ______ man in town. (rich)
richest

4. Your composition is the ______ of all. (bad)
worst

5. She is ______ than her sister. (beautiful)
more beautiful

6. This is the ______ tree in the garden. (tall)
tallest

7. He was carrying the ______ load of all. (heavy)
heaviest

8. The water of this well is ______. (sweet)
sweet

9. She is a ______ woman. (wise)
wise

10. This is the ______ question of all. (difficult)
most difficult

11. Prevention is ______ than cure. (good)
better

12. She is ______ than her elder sister. (wise)
wiser

13. He is the ______ of all the brothers. (tall)
tallest

14. She is the ______ girl I have ever seen. (sweet)
sweetest

lessons.title: Articles - a, an, the
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Use the for a definite or known thing - "The cat is a loving animal."
  • Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound - "a cup", "a child".
  • Use no article before uncountable nouns - "We write on paper.", "I like butter.", "I eat bread."
  • Use a for one thing of a kind - "A child drinks milk.", "I want a cup of coffee."

Solved Exercises

1. ______ cat is a loving animal.
The

2. ______ table is made of wood.
The

3. ______ child drinks milk.
A

4. We eat rice with ______ spoon.
a

5. ______ mango has ______ sweet taste.
A, a

6. I want ______ cup of coffee.
a

7. We write on ______ paper.
No article is used. We write on paper. Paper is an uncountable noun, so no article is needed.

8. Please give me ______ piece of paper.
a

9. ______ door of ______ room is broken.
The, the

10. There is ______ chair in ______ corner.
a, the

11. We write with ______ pen.
a

12. We write ______ letter.
a

13. I like ______ butter.
No article is used. I like butter. Butter is an uncountable noun, so no article is needed.

14. I eat ______ bread.
No article is used. I eat bread. Bread is an uncountable noun, so no article is needed.

15. I am eating ______ piece of bread.
a

lessons.title: Supply Suitable Adjectives
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An adjective tells what kind, how many, or which one - "homeless man", "five fingers", "These mangoes".
  • Descriptive adjectives: homeless, orphan, interesting, big, woollen.
  • Adjectives of number and quantity: five, any, many, All.
  • Demonstrative adjectives point out: These mangoes are sour.

These

lessons.title: Present Tenses
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Simple present is used for habits and facts - "She loves her cat very much."
  • Present continuous is used for an action happening now - "The baby is crying for milk now."
  • Present perfect is used for a past action with a present result - "He has stood first in the class."
  • Present perfect continuous is used for an action going on since a past time - "She has been working in this office for seven years."
  • Use since for a point of time and for for a period of time.

Solved Exercises

1. She (love) her cat very much.
She loves her cat very much.

2. He (go) to school everyday.
He goes to school everyday.

3. It (rain) at present.
It is raining at present.

4. They (take) tea every morning.
They take tea every morning.

5. Good students always (work) hard.
Good students always work hard.

6. The earth (revolve) around the sun.
The earth revolves around the sun.

7. She (learn) French at present.
She is learning French at present.

8. They (not do) their work regularly.
They do not do their work regularly.

9. Shahida (sing) a sad song today.
Shahida is singing a sad song today.

10. They always (come) back home late.
They always come back home late.

11. She (speak) English now.
She is speaking English now.

12. She (speak) English quite well.
She speaks English quite well.

13. The baby (cry) for milk now.
The baby is crying for milk now.

14. They (go) to sleep at ten.
They go to sleep at ten.

15. He (not keep) me waiting.
He is not keeping me waiting.

16. I already (take) three cups of coffee.
I have already taken three cups of coffee.

17. I (not see) you since Monday.
I have not seen you since Monday.

18. My brother (not write) to me for ten years.
My brother has not written to me for ten years.

19. She (learn) French for over two years.
She has been learning French for over two years.

20. The book (lie) on the table for weeks.
The book has been lying on the table for weeks.

21. He (not speak) to me since March.
He has not spoken to me since March.

22. She (sleep) since morning.
She has been sleeping since morning.

23. How long you (wait) here?
How long have you been waiting here?

24. He (stand) in the sun for an hour.
He has been standing in the sun for an hour.

25. She (work) in this office for seven years.
She has been working in this office for seven years.

26. They (not eat) anything since morning.

27. They already (do) their home task.
They have already done their home task.

28. I already (post) the letter.
I have already posted the letter.

29. The fire (burn) at night for two hours.
The fire has been burning at night for two hours.

30. You (rest) since morning.
You have been resting since morning.

lessons.title: Past Tenses
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Simple past is used for a finished past action - "The light went out when we were having dinner."
  • Past continuous is used for an action in progress at a past time - "She was singing a song when I entered the room."
  • Past perfect is used for the earlier of two past actions - "She had asked why we had wanted to leave early."
  • Past perfect continuous is used for an action that had been going on before a past time - "Ali had been preparing for his examination since October."

Solved Exercises

1. It (begin) to rain an hour ago.
It began to rain an hour ago.

2. How long ago you (come) here?
How long ago did you come here?

3. She (not hear) any noise.
She did not hear any noise.

4. He (ride) a bike when he (meet) an accident.
He was riding a bike when he met an accident.

5. He (leave) twenty minutes ago.
He left twenty minutes ago.

6. I (go) to airport when I (see) her.
I was going to airport when I saw her.

7. The light (go out) when we (have) dinner.
The light went out when we were having dinner.

8. She (sing) a song when I (enter) the room.
She was singing a song when I entered the room.

9. I (meet) her in the plane.
I met her in the plane.

10. I (make) tea when the door bell (ring).
I was making tea when the door bell rang.

11. He (not reply) to my letter.
He did not reply to my letter.

12. I (buy) this motor bike only a month ago.
I bought this motor bike only a month ago.

13. I (not listen) when you (talk).
I was not listening when you were talking.

14. The farmer (plough) the field when it (start) raining.
The farmer was ploughing the field when it started raining.

15. The bus (move) while I (board) it.
The bus was moving while I boarded it.

16. After you (leave) I went to sleep.
After you had left, I went to sleep.

17. They (take) their breakfast after they had washed their hands.
They had taken their breakfast after they had washed their hands.

18. I (work) on this assignment for a month.
I had been working on this assignment for a month.

19. Ali (prepare) for his examination since October.
Ali had been preparing for his examination since October.

20. She (ask) why we had wanted to leave early.
She had asked why we had wanted to leave early.

21. I asked her what places she (visit) in Europe.
I asked her what places she had visited in Europe.

22. The sun (not rise) before we were ready to leave.
The sun had not risen before we were ready to leave.

23. I had never seen snow before I (go) to Murree.
I had never seen snow before I went to Murree.

24. Aslam (swim) for three hours.
Aslam had been swimming for three hours.

25. The bus (stop) before we stepped out.
The bus had stopped before we stepped out.

lessons.title: Future Tenses
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Simple future uses will / shall - "I shall explain this to you."
  • Future continuous is used for an action in progress at a future time - "They will be travelling all night."
  • Future perfect is used for an action that will be finished by a future time - "The meeting will have ended by the time we gather."
  • Use by with a future time for the future perfect - "by the evening", "by the next fall".

Solved Exercises

12. She (return) from the tour of Europe by the middle of December next.

13. The farmers (reap) the harvest before the rains.

14. These mangoes (reach) the market by April.
These mangoes will have reached the market by April.

15. I (read) all the novels of Golding by the end of summer vacation.
I shall have read all the novels of Golding by the end of summer vacation.

16. The meeting (end) by the time we gather.
The meeting will have ended by the time we gather.

17. I hope it (stop) raining by the evening.
I hope it will have stopped raining by the evening.

18. She (take) her examination by the next fall.

19. They (complete) their work by tomorrow.

lessons.title: Change into Passive Voice
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In the passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
  • Use be + past participle - "Apples are liked by her."
  • The doer is shown with by - "by him", "by them".
  • The tense does not change - past stays past, perfect stays perfect.
  • In the passive, "He had told me to do it." becomes "I had been told by him to do it."

Solved Exercises

1. She likes apples.
Apples are liked by her.

2. The boy is climbing the wall.
The wall is being climbed by the boy.

3. We did not hear a sound.
No sound was heard by us.

4. They have bought a horse.
A horse has been bought by them.

5. The Board has given me a gold medal.
I have been given a gold medal by the Board.

6. He praised the boy for his courage.
The boy was praised by him for his courage.

7. The teacher was helping the students.
The students were being helped by the teacher.

8. Why were they beating the boy?
Why was the boy being beaten by them?

9. They have not done their job.
Their job has not been done by them.

10. A car ran over an old man.
An old man was run over by a car.

11. He will give you a box of chocolates.
You will be given a box of chocolates by him.

12. He had told me to do it.
I had been told by him to do it.

13. They had not done their home task.
Their home task had not been done by them.

14. We shall have finished our work by March next.
Our work will have been finished by us by March next.

15. He took away my books.
My books were taken away by him.

16. The sudden noise frightened the child.
The child was frightened by the sudden noise.

17. We use milk for making cheese.
Milk is used for making cheese by us.

18. Why is he mending the chair?

lessons.title: Stories from Outlines 1-3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Read the outline carefully and keep the events in the same order.
  • Write the story in the past tense with short, clear sentences.
  • Give the story a suitable title and end it with a moral.
  • Use connecting words - then, after that, at last - to join the events.

Outline 1 - A dog steals a piece of meat, runs...

Outline

A dog steals a piece of meat, runs away, comes to a bridge, sees his reflection in the calm water, thinks it is another dog with a bigger piece, barks at it, and loses his own piece as well.

Developed Story

A greedy dog once stole a piece of meat from a butcher's shop and ran away with it. On his way home he came to a bridge over a stream. The water under the bridge was calm and clear, and in it the dog saw his own reflection.

He thought it was another dog with a bigger piece of meat. Greedy for more, he barked at the reflection to snatch it. As he opened his mouth, his own piece of meat fell into the water and was lost.

Moral: Greed loses all.

Outline 2 - A hungry fox reaches a garden, sees bunches...

Outline

A hungry fox reaches a garden, sees bunches of ripe grapes hanging down a high wall, tries again and again but cannot reach them, and goes away disappointed.

Developed Story

A hungry fox went about in search of food and reached a garden. There he saw bunches of ripe grapes hanging down from a high wall. He jumped again and again to reach them, but the grapes were too high and he could not get at them.

At last, tired and disappointed, he went away saying, The grapes are sour. Moral: People often blame what they cannot get.

Outline 3 - A merchant earns a large sum of money,...

Outline

A merchant earns a large sum of money, has to go a long way, a nail falls from his horse's shoe, the inn boy warns him, he does not care, the horse becomes lame, and robbers kill him and take the money.

Developed Story

A merchant earned a large sum of money by selling his goods and had to travel a long way home. As it was already getting dark, a nail fell from his horse's shoe. The inn boy warned him to get it fixed, but the merchant did not care and hurried away.

Soon the horse became lame, and robbers appeared, killed him and made away with the money. Moral: A stitch in time saves nine.

Outline 4 - A tiger kills a woman with a gold...

Outline

A tiger kills a woman with a gold bangle and keeps it. One day a man comes to a stream, the tiger pretends to be pious and offers the bangle, and the greedy man falls prey to the tiger.

Developed Story

A tiger once killed a woman and kept her gold bangle. One day a man came to the bank of a stream and was getting ready to cross it when the tiger appeared. The man was afraid, but the tiger told him that it had become pious and spent its time in prayer, and offered him the bangle.

The greedy man went near to take it and fell prey to the tiger. Moral: Greed leads to ruin; never trust a wicked person.

Outline 5 - A flock of pigeons sees food grain in...

Outline

A flock of pigeons sees food grain in the fields, lands against their chief's warning, is caught in a net, and escapes by pulling the net up together.

Developed Story

A flock of pigeons was flying over vast green fields when they looked down and saw plenty of food grain. They asked their chief to alight, but he did not agree, fearing that a hunter might have set a net there. The pigeons said his fear was imaginary, landed, and were caught in the net.

They cried, O chief, what shall we do now? He said, Dear friends, now exert together; pull the net up and fly away with it. They followed his advice and were saved.

Moral: Union is strength.

Outline 6 - A kind man frees a tiger caught in...

Outline

A kind man frees a tiger caught in a trap, the tiger attacks him, and a clever jackal gets the tiger back into the cage.

Developed Story

A kind-hearted man was passing through a forest when he found a tiger caught in a trap. The tiger begged for help, and though the man was afraid of the beast, at last he set it free. At once the tiger knocked him down.

The man called the tiger ungrateful, and both went to a pipal tree for its opinion. The tree said man was ungrateful. They went to a bullock, which upheld the tree's decision.

Next they asked a jackal. The jackal said it could not believe that so big a beast could be contained in so small a cage. The tiger jumped into the cage to prove it, the jackal shut the cage, and the man went away thanking the jackal.

Moral: Wisdom is better than strength.

Outline 7 - A farmer has four lazy sons, tells them...

Outline

A farmer has four lazy sons, tells them of a treasure buried in the fields, and after his death they dig the field and get a bumper crop.

Developed Story

A farmer had four lazy sons who did nothing. He advised them to work, but they did not follow his advice. When the farmer fell seriously ill, he called all his sons and told them of a treasure lying buried somewhere in the fields, and then passed away.

His sons dug the whole field deep, and though they found no treasure, they got a bumper crop. Then they realised the wisdom of their father and became rich. Moral: Hard work is the real treasure.

lessons.notes_html:
Outline 8 - A young cricket sings all spring and summer,...

Outline

A young cricket sings all spring and summer, starves in winter, begs food from an ant, and is refused.

Developed Story

A young cricket sang merrily throughout spring and summer. When winter came, snow covered everything and there was no food. The cricket began to starve and went to an ant living close by to beg for food.

The ant said, We ants neither lend nor borrow. It asked the cricket why it had not stored food for winter in summer. The cricket replied, I sang away the summer.

The ant said, Now dance away the winter. No work, no food. Moral: Work today for tomorrow.

Outline 9 - A rich man in a carriage is attacked...

Outline

A rich man in a carriage is attacked by wolves in a forest, and his faithful servant fights them off while the family escapes.

Developed Story

A rich man was riding in a four-horse carriage with his family and a servant when he passed through a forest. Hungry wolves attacked them. The man let loose two horses one by one, but the wolves came up again.

Then the faithful servant drew his sword, jumped down and fought with the wolves. The rich man and his family gained time and escaped. Moral: Faithfulness is a great virtue.

Outline 10 - A lion terrorises the animals, a hare tricks...

Outline

A lion terrorises the animals, a hare tricks him by showing him his own reflection in a well, and the lion is drowned.

Developed Story

A lion killed many animals, and all the animals were terrified. A hare offered to save them. He reached the lion's den late, and the lion asked in rage why he was so late.

The hare told the lion of another lion who had stopped him. The lion asked the hare to take him to the other lion. The hare took him to a well, the lion saw his reflection, jumped down to fight it, and was drowned.

Moral: Wisdom wins over strength.

lessons.title: Paragraphs from Outlines 1-4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A paragraph has one main idea - every sentence supports it.
  • Begin with a topic sentence, then give details in order, then close the paragraph.
  • Write in simple, clear sentences of about 100 to 150 words.
  • Keep the events and facts in the order given in the outline.

Outline 1 - A Fortune-teller....

Outline

A Fortune-teller.

Developed Paragraph

A footpath fortune-teller sits with his books and cards in a basket and a pencil tucked on his ear, and a parrot in a cage beside him. In fact, the parrot is the real fortune-teller. The fortune-teller is a big fraud who cleverly manipulates simple people, village men and women, who are his clients.

He poses as a serious, knowledgeable man and pretends to know the movement of the stars, like an astrologer. The illiterate people feel satisfied when he tells them that they will have a job, a wife, a son, a cart, a seven marla house, a twelve acre farm or a tractor.

Outline 2 - A Picnic....

Outline

A Picnic.

Developed Paragraph

The rainy season had set in and all around it was lush green when we went out for a picnic at Jallo Park. It was a family affair. We cooked our meals out there in the sprawling park, with trees and bushes all around and lakes nearby.

The drive along the Canal Bank was fascinating, with flowering trees all along the canal and unpolluted air. We played badminton, ran around, inhaled fresh air, and had sizzling snacks with tea in the afternoon. We enjoyed the return drive along the clean and green Canal Bank.

Outline 3 - A Street Quarrel....

Outline

A Street Quarrel.

Developed Paragraph

I was having my evening meal in the main street of Gowalmandi when I heard a terrible noise out in the street. I got up and looked out. About fifty persons were standing in front of a big shop, and four or five persons ran out of the shop and exchanged violent blows.

The cause was an old enmity. It was a sad spectacle to see neighbours fighting in the street instead of living in peace.

Outline 4 - A Visit to a Historical Place....

Outline

A Visit to a Historical Place.

Developed Paragraph

We visited the Shalimar Garden, whose main entrance was closed to traffic. After buying entry tickets we entered the first terrace, vast and lush green. A brief description of the garden was given at the entry door.

There were small brick paths with a long row of fountains in the middle and ornamental lights in the flower beds, with old mango trees on both sides. The massive boundary wall, the royal enclosure and the marble throne on the second terrace, a big pool of water with sidewalks and a middle path connecting the two royal enclosures, and the third terrace with bushes and trees all around, made it a rare specimen of Mughal architecture.

lessons.title: Paragraphs from Outlines 5-8
lessons.notes_html:
Outline 5 - A Visit to a Zoo....

Outline

A Visit to a Zoo.

Developed Paragraph

We visited the Lahore Zoo, where huge models of an elephant and three other animals are mounted at the main entry on Shahrah-e-Quaid-e-Azam. There was a beautiful waterfall at the side of the animals' cages and a renovated booking office with rock walls. In the monkey cages with swings, visitors were feeding the monkeys grams.

We enjoyed the elephant ride, saw the monster-like hippopotamus in a huge pond which raised its large head and muzzled so that children ran helter-skelter, the fearful rhinoceros with two upright horns above its nose, the lion and the lioness, the king of the zoo as well, in big and strong cages, and peacocks, the graceful zebra with black and white stripes, parrots, ducks and flamingos, and the wonderful giraffe with a long neck.

Outline 6 - Allama Iqbal....

Outline

Allama Iqbal.

Developed Paragraph

Allama Iqbal was an eminent philosopher and poet, born in 1877 at Sialkot. He received his school and early college education at Murray College, where Syed Mir Hassan was his inspiring teacher of Persian and Urdu. He took his Master's degree from Government College Lahore and went to England and Germany for higher studies.

On his return he gave a new direction to Muslim thought and wrote poems in praise of Muslim culture. He awakened the Muslims and gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in the sub-continent. His books like Bang-e-Dra, Bal-e-Jibril, Asrar-e-Khudi and Payam-e-Mashriq inspired the Muslims' imagination.

The nation pays glorious tribute to him every year, and he is buried beside the Badshahi Masjid in Lahore.

Outline 7 - The Teacher I Like the Best....

Outline

The Teacher I Like the Best.

Developed Paragraph

It is but natural to have a strong liking for somebody. I have respect and reverence for all teachers, but Mr Mazhar-ul-Haq is the teacher I like the best. He has a charming personality, is elegantly dressed, and holds M.A. and B.Ed. degrees.

He is punctual and diligent and teaches English with confidence and correct pronunciation. He is well-read, a patriot and public-spirited, maintains perfect discipline during lessons, encourages students to ask questions, does not lose his temper, praises hard-working students, and makes lessons interesting with anecdotes. He is broad-minded and dignified, a beloved teacher indeed.

Outline 8 - A House on Fire....

Outline

A House on Fire.

Developed Paragraph

It was a perfectly peaceful night and winter had set in, with only the occasional bark of a street dog, when there was an abrupt commotion out in the street, echoing steps and cries of fire, fire. I leapt out and saw that about a hundred steps ahead, the upper storey of a house was on fire. Some women were wailing outside, billows of smoke were dense and choking, and neighbours with pails of water were eager to lend a helping hand.

The inmates were safely brought down. Then the fire brigade arrived with a ladder and water hose, and the leaping flames subsided. Curtains, furniture, carpets and wooden almirahs were completely burnt.

There was loss of property but no loss of life.

lessons.notes_html:
Note: The source PDF gives the questions and answers only. The passage text itself is not printed in the source - read the passage in the printed book.

Key Points

  • Read the passage carefully before answering the questions.
  • Answer in complete sentences and in your own words.
  • Give the fact asked for - a name, a reason, or a result - and nothing extra.

Exercise 1 - Choice of a profession

Q1. What were the conditions about the choice of a profession sixty years ago?
About sixty years ago, the choice of a profession was not taken up seriously, and a son generally followed the trade of his father.

Q2. Why did the people not choose the profession seriously?
Because sons generally followed their fathers' trades, and there was no thought of choosing a profession by one's own liking and aptitude.

Q3. Can a student of the present times choose his profession freely?
Yes, nowadays one can take up a trade that one likes.

Q4. What is the advantage of a right choice of a profession?
The students who make the right choice of profession are always successful.

Q5. How can a student choose his profession rightly?
He should have some definite aim, and take guidance from his teacher and parents, who study his habits and guide him to the right path of life.

Q6. What will be the difficulty of a student who is reading without a definite aim?
He suffers a lot in the end, as he has difficulty in finding employment.

Q7. How can a teacher help his pupils in making a choice of profession?
The teacher keeps an eye on his pupils and studies their habits, so he can guide his pupils to the right path of life.

Exercise 2 - Making pottery

Q1. What is throwing?
Making pottery on the potter's wheel is called throwing.

Q2. What is the other method of shaping articles?
Moulding: a plaster mould is made and the clay is pressed into it.

Q3. What is the advantage of moulding?
It is a quicker and less difficult way to make things like handles.

Q4. How does the potter make designs on the pieces of pottery?
When a piece of pottery is taken off the wheel, it is put aside to dry, after which a design is painted on it with special colours that will stand great heat.

Q5. How are the pieces of pottery baked in fire?
The pieces are placed in earthenware tubs called saggers, so that the flames cannot touch the pots, and then fired in a large oven or kiln.

Exercise 3 - The Sultan's library

Q1. Why did the Sultan send his agents to all parts of the East?
To buy rare manuscripts and bring them back to Cordova for his library.

Q2. Where and why did they search the booksellers' shops?
At Cairo, Damascus and Baghdad, searching the booksellers' shops for rare volumes for his library.

Q3. What would he do when any book could not be bought at any price?
He would have it copied.

Q4. What would he do when the author had not yet written the book?
He would send the author a handsome present and beg him to send the first copy to Cordova.

Q5. How many books had he gathered?
No fewer than four hundred thousand books.

Q6. Why was it difficult to collect so many books in those days?
Printing was unknown at that time, and every copy had to be painfully copied in the fine clear hand of the professional copyist.

Exercise 4 - Musa, commander-in-chief

Q1. Who was the chief commander and what was in his charge?
Musa was the chief commander, and the gates were in his charge.

Q2. When were the gates barred?
When the Christians came in view.

Q3. Who threw them open?
Musa threw them open.

Q4. What did Musa say?
Our bodies will bar the gates. He also said: We have nothing to fight for but the ground we stand on, and without that we are without a home or a country.

Q5. What effect had his words on the young men?
The young men were kindled by his words and were ready to die with him, performing feats of bravery.

Exercise 5 - Early rising

Q1. What kind of habit is early rising?
Early rising is a good habit.

Q2. Why can an early riser do more work than the late riser?
Because he gains time while the late risers are asleep, and has plenty of time to do his work carefully, steadily and completely.

Q3. What kind of health do early risers have?
Good and sound health.

Q4. Why does a late riser find his work dull and dry?
Because he gets up late and does his duty unwillingly, finding it dull and dry.

Q5. What is the key to success in life?
Early rising is the key to success in life.

Exercise 6 - Social ants

Q1. What do we mean by social insects?
Social insects are insects that live in societies, cooperate with one another and do only the work assigned to them.

Q2. Why are some ants called social insects?
Because they live in societies and cooperate with one another.

Q3. How do the ants cooperate with one another?
They go out in search of food in an orderly fashion, marching in lines and columns like soldiers.

Q4. What principle do they follow while doing their work?
They manage their affairs through division of labour.

Q5. Why are the members of a certain group called soldier ants?
Because they guard and protect their community and fight with other insects who attack them or raid their colony.

Q6. How have the ants learnt the principle of division of labour?
They have not learnt it; they have inherited it.

Exercise 7 - Allama Muhammad Iqbal

Q1. Why is Allama Muhammad Iqbal considered to be one of the greatest poets of all times?
Because he wrote as many great poems as very few poets did, and he was much more than a poet: a learned man, a great scholar and philosopher, and a political leader of great importance.

Q2. Did he write poetry for poetry's sake?
No, he did not write poetry for poetry's sake.

Q3. How can you say that Allama Muhammad Iqbal was much more than a mere poet?
He was a learned man, a great scholar and philosopher, and a political leader of great importance, besides being a poet.

Q4. What kind of Muslim was Allama Muhammad Iqbal?
He was a Muslim who had a great love for Allah and His Rasool.

Q5. With what aim did he write poetry?
He wrote poetry to express the great and everlasting truths of philosophy, history and Islam.

Q6. What was Allama Muhammad Iqbal's call to the Muslims of the whole world?
To awake the Muslims of the whole world from their deep sleep and to unite.

Exercise 8 - The girl and the coin

Q1. What did the girl find?
A coin.

Q2. When did she find it?
When she was sweeping the yard; it rolled away before her broom and fell with a little clatter against the wall.

Q3. How had the coin been dropped there?
Someone had dropped it while crossing the yard and perhaps had not even troubled to look for it.

Q4. What was the worth of the coin?
It was worth little.

Q5. Why was it a whole fortune for her?
Because she never had anything of her own before, so it seemed a whole fortune to her.

Q6. How did she clean it?
She rubbed it clean on the sleeve of her blue cotton jacket.

Q7. What did she do after cleaning it?
She put it into her pocket.

Exercise 9 - Iqbal's Allahabad address

Q1. Where was the annual meeting of All India Muslim League held in 1930?
At Allahabad.

Q2. Who was invited to preside over the session?
Dr Muhammad Iqbal was invited to preside over the session.

Q3. What idea did Allama Iqbal oppose?
He openly opposed the idea of power-sharing between Hindus and Muslims as one nation.

Q4. Which provinces did he want to be included in the Muslim state?
The Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Q5. On what grounds did he demand a separate state for the Muslims of India?
So that the Muslims should live according to the teachings of Islam; applying one constitution to both Hindus and Muslims would result in a civil war.

Q6. When was the Pakistan Resolution adopted?
In 1940, when the Pakistan Resolution was adopted.

Exercise 10 - The Indian National Congress

Q1. Who founded the Indian National Congress?
Mr A.O. Hume, a liberal Englishman.

Q2. Who was Mr A.O. Hume?
He had joined the Indian Civil Service in 1849 and retired after shouldering different responsibilities.

Q3. When was the Indian National Congress founded?
In 1885.

Q4. Why did Hume think of founding this political organisation?
He had been watching the ugly law and order situation and believed the high-handed rule of the Britishers was paving the way for an unexpected outburst of violence. His plan was a safety valve to minimise the mounting sentiments against British rule and to ventilate the revolutionary spirit.

Q5. With whom did he discuss his plan?
He put his plan before Lord Dufferin.

Q4. What was in the vessel?
Grains.

Q5. What did the monkey do?

Q6. Why could he not pull his hand out of the vessel?

Q7. How did the monkey meet his fate?

Exercise 13 - The tailor and the elephant

Q1. Where did the elephant go everyday?

Q2. What did the tailor give him?

Q3. What mistake did the tailor make one day?

Q4. What did the elephant do after drinking water?

Q5. How did the elephant punish the tailor for his mistake?

Tit for tat: as you sow, so shall you reap. Do not annoy others, for kindness is repaid with kindness and mischief with mischief.

Exercise 14 - Professional and amateur players

Q1. What is meant by professional player?
A professional player is one whose main aim is to make money; he plays the game to earn money or win a name.

Q2. With what aim does he play games?
To earn money or win a name.

Q3. What makes an amateur player a responsible citizen?
He plays honestly, observes all the rules and regulations of games, and accepts defeat without cheating or unfair means, so he becomes a disciplined gentleman and a responsible citizen.

Q4. What qualities of true sportsmanship does a professional player lack?
True sportsmanship: playing for pleasure, honesty, observing the rules, and accepting defeat gracefully.

Q5. How does an amateur player differ from a professional player?
The amateur plays because he gets pleasure in playing, and games give him recreation and physical exercise; the professional plays to earn money or win a name.

Q6. How does an amateur player take his defeat?

The amateur player.

Exercise 15 - The camel

Q1. Why is the camel called the ship of the desert?
Because it is the best means of transport in deserts, going on walking for hours on the burning sand and in the blazing sun.

It can go without food and water for days and weeks.

It can store food and water; its hump is also a store of food, which the camel uses when it gets nothing to eat and drink for many days.

lessons.title: Story Specimens 1-4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A story has a beginning, a middle, and an end - keep the events in order.
  • Write in the past tense and use dialogue to make the story lively.
  • Every story in this chapter ends with a clear moral - learn it with the story.

A Farmer and His Sons

Once a farmer had three grown-up sons. They always quarrelled among themselves. Their father advised them to live in peace but it had no effect on them.

He was worried about their future. One day the farmer fell seriously ill. He sent for his sons.

He asked them to collect a handful of sticks which they did at once. He tied the sticks into a bundle. Now, he asked them to break the bundle one by one.

They tried hard to break it but none could. At last, the farmer untied the bundle and asked each of them to break each stick. They did so quite easily.

Their father said, "My dear sons, you could not break the sticks as long as they remained tied together but you broke each single stick quite easily. They were strong in bundle but became weak when separated from one another. Never forget that united we stand and divided we fall." This had a deep effect on the farmer's sons.

They gave up quarrelling and began to live in peace.

The Kindness of Rasoolullah

Once the Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) went out on a journey along with some of his companions. Birds were singing and chirping joyfully. One of the companions of the Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) saw a nest in a bush.

It was the nest of sparrows and there were two sparrow chicks in it. He picked up the young sparrow. All at once the sparrows came crying and began to fly over his head.

The Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) asked his companion why the sparrows were circling over his head. He told the Rasoolullah(peace be upon him) that he had removed their young ones from their nest. The Rasoolullah(peace be upon him) was greatly moved.

He (peace be upon him) felt sorry for the poor little birds and advised his companion to put back the sparrow's chick in its nest at once, which he did. The sparrows felt happy and cried no more. The Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) was kind and affectionate not only to human beings but also to all creatures of the universe.

For this very reason Allah Almighty was pleased to bestow upon him (peace be upon him) the title of 'Benefactor of all the worlds.' The Rasoolullah (peace be upon him), kind to others, also said, "Allah will not be kind to him who is not

Robbers Turn into Good Citizens

Hazrat Sheikh Abdul Qadir Gillani (may Allah have mercy on him) had to undertake a journey, when he was yet a young boy. His pious mother stitched up forty gold coins in his shirt. She advised her son to always speak the truth.

He joined a caravan and set off on his journey. When the caravan entered a forest, a gang of robbers fell on the travellers and deprived them of all their valuables. While they were busy robbing everyone, a robber happened to pass by the young boy.

He said, "Do you have anything on you?" "Yes," came the prompt reply, "I have forty gold coins." The robber asked the young boy to show the money, which he readily did. The robber took the boy to the leader of the gang. Like all other robbers, the leader was also surprised.

He said, "Why did you not deny having money?" Hazrat Sheikh Abdul Qadir Gillani (may Allah have mercy on him) told the robbers' Chief that his mother had advised him to speak the truth always. This had a deep effect on the Chief. He said, "Alas!

I do not obey the commands of Allah while this little boy so faithfully follows the advice of his mother." Remorse became a guideline to show him the right path. He made up his mind to give up his bad ways of earning livelihood. He disbanded the gang and advised all the members to live an honest life.

Thus, the example set by Hazrat Sheikh Abdul Qadir Gillani (may Allah have mercy on him) reformed all the robbers. He grew up to be a great religious leader and a pious saint. He is held in great esteem by millions of his followers and devotees.

He is popularly known as Ghaus-ul-Azam Gillani. Moral: Speak the truth always.

The Muslim Brotherhood

Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) united the Muslims into a wonderful brotherhood. They were sincerely devoted to one another and made every sacrifice for other Muslims whoever and wherever they might be. They laid down their lives for their Muslim brethren.

Abu Jahan Bin Huzefa (peace be upon him) told us a wonderful story. It is a true story, related to the battle of Yarmook, which showed their great love and sense of sacrifice for one another. He said, "I set out in search of my cousin who was fighting on the battle front.

I carried a water-skin to offer water to the thirsty soldiers. I found him lying seriously injured. He was about to die.

I asked him if he wanted water. My cousin nodded. I offered him a cup of water.

Just then there came a cry for water from Hisham ibn al-A'as (peace be upon him) who was about to die. My cousin asked me to give the cup to him. When I came to Hisham (peace be upon him) , another cry was heard from a mujahid, not far from the former two.

Hisham (peace be upon him) asked me to take the cup to him. I, therefore, went to the third one but he had breathed his last before he could drink. I hurried back to Hisham (peace be upon him) .

He (peace be upon him) had also lost his life. Then I rushed back to my cousin but he too had left for his heavenly home." How great those good Muslims were indeed! In true spirit of Islam, Muslims worry about their brothers selflessly.

lessons.title: Story Specimens 5-8
lessons.notes_html:
A Foolish Stag

One hot summer day, a stag went to a pool to drink water. The pool water was clear. It could see its reflection in the water.

It felt proud of its beautiful horns. But when it saw the shadow of its thin legs, it felt sad and hated them. While it was still thinking of its ugly legs, it heard the sound of the horse's hoofs of a huntsman and the barking of hounds.

It ran for its life as fast as its legs could carry it. In no time it left the hounds far behind. Now it happened to pass through a thick forest.

As it rushed through, its horns got caught in the branches of a tree. It struggled hard to free itself but all in vain. Meanwhile, the hunter and his hounds came close.

The hounds were about to catch it, the stag struggled and managed to escape. The legs it hated had carried it away from the hounds. One of the horns broke but it managed to dodge the hunter.

After loosing the hunter, the stag was grateful of having thin legs and did not repent the appearance again.. Moral: Be grateful of what you have

The Donkey Trapped in His Own Trick

A villager had a donkey. He earned his living by transporting goods from place to place on that donkey. One early morning, he loaded the donkey with salt and set off to the town.

A stream ran across his way to the market. As the donkey walked through the stream it slipped and fell down. A good deal of salt was washed away and the donkey felt light.

The donkey thought it was quite a good trick to make the load light. Next morning, the man again loaded it with salt. The donkey played the same trick and got light.

The master saw through the game and made up his mind to teach the donkey a good lesson. Now, on the third day he put a bale of cotton on the donkey. The silly animal tried the same trick once more.

Soaked with water, the cotton load became much heavier than when it was dry. Moral: The foolish donkey was punished for his bad intention..

A Friend in Need is a Friend Indeed

Once upon a time two very close friends lived in a village. As time passed their friendship grew stronger. Now they were grown up men.

One day they decided to go and find work. They set off. Before leaving their village, they promised to stand by each other through thick and thin.

They took oath of sincerity and assured each other of help in the hour of need. They had to pass through a jungle. They had not gone far into the thick forest when they found themselves face to face with a big bear.

The beast began to move towards them. They felt helpless and terrified. One of them knew how to climb a tree.

He at once caught hold of a strong branch and swung up the tree. The other could not climb. He had heard that the bear does not eat the dead.

So he lay down on the ground and held his breath pretending to be dead. Meanwhile, the bear came to him and sniffed him. The beast left him.

When the bear had gone out of sight, the friend on the tree came down. He asked his friend, "Dear friend, what did the bear whisper in your ear?" The other replied quickly, "The bear advised me not to trust a selfish friend." Saying this he left him and went away.

A Faithful Friend

A hunter had a beautiful hound that always went hunting with him. The faithful dog was a fast friend of the hunter's only son who loved to play with the dog. The master also loved the hound for its friendship with his young son who was only ten years old.

The master of the house had no one else in the house. One day, the hunter went out hunting but forgot to take the hound with him. His son was still asleep in his bed.

As he reached the edge of the forest he found that he had forgotten to bring the hound with him. He decided to go back and bring the hound. He came home but was afraid to see his hound all bloodstained standing at the gate.

The hunter thought that the hound had harmed his son. He got very upset and tensed and chained it.. He quickly walked into the house and looked high and low for his son.

Just then, he saw his son coming out of his room. The boy told his father that a wolf had come into the house and was about to kill him when the hound pounced upon it and tore it to pieces. The hunter began to cry and rushed back to the gate and took the hound to a vet.

The hunter loved the hound as his most loyal friend.

lessons.title: Story Specimens 9-12
lessons.notes_html:
A Big Reward

Once a hungry wolf was devouring his prey. In a bid to finish it quickly, he swallowed a big bite of the flesh but a bone also went in and got stuck in his throat. It hurt him very much.

So he decided to go to a crane to get help from him. He said, "Well dear friend, I am in a great trouble. Please pick out the bone in my throat." The crane was afraid lest the wolf should bite off his head.

But the wolf assured him of safety and a big reward besides, for the service. At last, the crane agreed to do the needful. It put its long beak into the throat of the wolf and pulled out the bone.

The wolf was very happy now. The crane demanded the promised reward for his service. The wolf, at once, said, "Isn't it a big reward that I have not bitten off your head when it could not have escaped my teeth."The crane hopped away disappointedly.

The Tailor and the Elephant

A tailor ran a shop in a town. He was a good natured jolly fellow. A man in the town had a pet elephant.

The elephant went drinking at a pool out of the town daily. It passed by the tailor's shop. The tailor gave him a bun every day.

In course of time, they became good friends and were well pleased to meet each other. The tailor always waited for the elephant to come to him and the elephant was also there at the usual time. One day, the tailor had a dispute with one of his customers.

He was feeling unhappy and cross. Meanwhile, the elephant arrived and put his trunk into his shop through the window to receive the friendly bun as usual. The tailor instead of giving a bun, pricked its trunk with a needle.

The elephant felt hurt at this but silently went his way to drink. The elephant quenched his thirst and then filled his trunk with dirty, muddy water. It came back quickly, put its trunk in, and emptied it.

The whole shop looked as if it was plastered with mud. All the fancy dresses and rich wedding robes were mud-stained and badly spoiled. The tailor was sad but it was too late.

Moral: It is well said, "Look before you leap."

The Boy Who Cried "Wolf "

There lived a shepherd boy in a village near a pasture. He collected sheep and goats belonging to the villagers and took them to the pasture to graze. This went on for quite a long time.

All the villagers were well satisfied with the boy as he tended the flock carefully. Now everyone trusted the boy. By now he had grown up into a fine lad.

One fine morning, when he was busy looking after animals, it came to his mind to make fun of the villagers. So, he climbed upto the top of the hill and cried aloud, "Wolf! Wolf!" the villagers rushed to the pasture to save the boy and the flock.

They came armed with sticks. When they saw the boy, they inquired about the wolf. The naughty boy began to laugh.

Everyone was angry with the silly boy and went back grumbling. After few days, the boy repeated his trick. The worried villagers rushed for his help and found the boy laughing on the villagers.

This time the villagers were highly displeased by him and decided again. One day the boy took sheep and goats to the pasture as per the routine. This time the wolf did come and he cried, 'Wolf' at top of his voice.

The villagers could hear his cries but they thought he was joking again. No one came to his help. The wolf not only killed some sheep and goats, but had injured the boy.

He learnt his lesson and never tricked anyone again. Moral: No one trusts a liar.

The Jester and the King

Once upon a time a king had a jester in his court. The king was so fond of him that the jester enjoyed every kind of liberty of speech. He did not even spare the lords and ministers.

So much so that he began to ridicule even the king but no one could dare to complain against him. This made the jester bold and proud. He cared for none.

One day while the king was holding a court and was busy in serious state affairs, the jester made fun of the king. Dead silence fell on the court. The king got highly offended and sentenced the jester to treason.

The jester bent down over his knees and begged for mercy but the king was so angry that he turned down his request. At last, when the jester pleaded for mercy again and again, the king said, "Die you must but I grant you the freedom to choose the kind of death you like." The clever jester at once used his ready wit and took good advantage of the concession saying, "Your Majesty! I choose to die of old age." The king was impressed and forgave the jester with a warning for future.

Moral: It never pays to overreach yourself.

lessons.title: Informal Letters i-viii
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An informal letter has: address, date, salutation, body, and subscription.
  • Write the address and date at the top, then "Dear ..." and the body in short paragraphs.
  • End with "Yours affectionately" or "Yours sincerely" and your name.
  • A formal invitation is short and formal; a reply accepts or declines it politely.
  • An application begins with the addressee, then "Sir," the request, and "Yours obediently".

Letter i - your mother who is worried about your health

2, Old Hostel, Lahore. March 23, 2017 Dear Mother, I received your letter yesterday. I am glad to know that you are fine. I was running a fever due to bad throat.

But it was a temporary ailment. I have recovered now. You need not worry about my health.

I am perfectly all right. I am taking good care of my diet and exercise regularly. I hope that after these assurances you will stop worrying about me.

Pay my regards to all at home. Yours affectionately, Naveed Ahmad

Letter ii - your father asking him about the health of your mother

2, Old Hostel, Lahore. January 25, 2017 Dear Father, From Ali's letter I have come to know that mother is suffering from high blood pressure. I am really worried about her. I hope that she is taking precautionary measures to bring it to normal.

Please ask her to take her medicine regularly and also inform me about her present condition as early as possible. Anxiously waiting for your reply, Yours affectionately, Nadeem

Letter iii - your sister congratulating her on her success in the exams

15 - C Wahdat Colony, Lahore. March 28, 2017 Dear Najma, Your letter brought the happy news of your excellent result in the final examination of class 9. I am very happy to learn that you have gottem an outstanding result. I am very proud of you.

You have always been a hard working student and I hope you will work even harder next year to maintain a high standard. Accept my heartiest congratulations on your success. Pay my compliments to Naila and other friends.

Yours affectionately, Afshan

Letter iv - your mother about the test you have just taken

92, Boys' Hostel, Gulberg, Lahore. February 06, 2017 Dear Mother, I am sorry, I did not write you earlier as I was busy preparing for my test of physics. It was held yesterday. My performance in the test is satisfactory.

I hope to get full marks in it. I attempted eleven questions. The answer to one question was wrong.

But it was an extra question. I hope that you are satisfied with my explanation now. Pay my regards to everyone at home.

Yours affectionately, Khalid Ahmad

Letter v - your father requesting him to send you some extra funds for the...

16, Crescent Hostel, Gulberg, Lahore. March 15, 2017 Dear Father, I have been planning to write you for many days but could not find time to do so. My exams are drawing near and I am busy preparing for them. I have already revised my course.

You need not worry about my studies. The only problem that I face these days is that I have run short of money as I bought some books which has upset my budget. I shall be very grateful if you send me at least ten thousand rupees to pay my hostel dues and to meet my other needs.

Yours affectionately, Anas Ali

Letter vi - your brother about the importance of the study of science...

10 - Jail Road, Lahore. March 01, 2017 Dear Asif, I hope this letter finds you in the best of health and spirits. You have now been promoted to class nine. It is time for you to decide whether you would like to study humanities or science subjects.

The world has progressed very much in the field of science. If we want to keep pace with it, we must keep our knowledge of science up-to-date. Everyone should know the basics of science so I would advise you to study science at least up to matriculation level.It will broaden the horizon of choice that you can make for higher studies Also, there are many new fields in science that might catch your interest.

Please think carefully before making a final decision. Convey my salaam to your friends. Yours affectionately, Adnan Bashir

Letter vii - your friend congratulating her on her birthday

18-Tariq Block, Garden Town, Lahore. January 29, 2017 Dear Iram, I am specially writing this letter to congratulate you on your birthday. I owe you a gift and you will get it when you come to Lahore. I was going to send it to you by post but then I was informed that you plan to come to Lahore. So I decided to give it to you personally. I am waiting for you.

Convey my respects to aunt and uncle. Wishing you the best, Yours sincerely, Samina

Letter viii - your friend requesting her to spend her spring holidays with you

13 - C, GOR-III, Lahore. February 6, 2017 Dear Sadia, You know that our spring holidays are approaching. I would like you to spend these holidays with me. In your last letter you promised to come to me during these holidays.

Now it is time to fulfill your promise. We shall visit our common friends and do some shopping. Inform me as early as possible about the exact date of your arrival so that I may make further arrangements accordingly.

With love, Yours sincerely, Shazia

lessons.title: Dialogue Specimens 1-2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people.
  • Write the speaker's name, then what the speaker says - keep each turn short and natural.
  • Use correct punctuation: question marks for questions and exclamation marks for strong feelings.

Dialogue between a teacher and a student

Teacher: Hello Fauzia! You are a bit late today.

Fauzia: Yes, Madam, I am sorry.

Teacher: Well. What happened?

Fauzia: The school bus was right on schedule. It was about to cross the canal bridge when it came to a halt with a jerk. The tyre had gone flat.

Teacher: I see. It is not your fault.

Fauzia: One thing more, Madam. The driver had no jack with him. He waved to other vehicles but they would not stop. Nobody seemed willing to oblige at this rush hour.

Teacher: Well. What did you do then? You came by another bus. Didn't you?

Fauzia: No, Madam, we left the bus where it was and walked up to school all the way.

Teacher: Well done! You are a brave girl indeed But remember, always be careful while crossing roads. Now, girls let us get going with our lesson.

Dialogue between two students regarding Salat

Osama: Well, now I'd like to take rest for a while. I've had my meal, you know.

Salman: Ok. You take rest while I fix this picture of a landscape on the wall. Where is the sticky tape?

Osama: Out there in the drawer.

Salman: Well, I think this picture needs to be a bit higher up. How do you like it Osama?

Osama: Lovely! Good, well done. It looks nice up there. Now let us go for namaz to the masjid.

Salman: I am going to the market. I shall not be long.

Osama: No, namaz first. Have you heard the moezzin's call for salat? Haven't you?

Salman: Sure, I have but I am going out. It's very urgent. My motor bike is out at the gate.

Osama: There is nothing in the world that ought to be more urgent than a namaz.

Salman: I don't really understand it. Art is long and life is short. There is so much to do in the world. There is so much fun-games, sports, T. V., cricket, world cups, videos, feature films, fun-fairs, shopping, loitering and break and break and break. Sorry, I am going.

Osama: Dear me! Who am I to hold you back? Dear as you are to me, I sincerely wish that you offer namaz. Namaz gives us peace, freshness, balance, courage, hope, goodness in our short life here on the earth, and eternal goodness in the life hereafter.

Salman: Oh, I am sick of your sermons, Osama!

Osama: See, Allah has given us eyes, ears, heart, hands, legs and brain. Salman, you see such a lovely world is there around us. Great gifts are they! Aren't they? We must thank Allah - the Merciful, the Sustainer. As Muslims we offer namaz and this is how we thank Allah.

Salman: All right. I must thank Allah for the blessings that He has bestowed upon me.I love Him, too. I'll go with you.

options: Because she missed the first bus

lessons.title: Dialogue Specimens 3-5
lessons.notes_html:
Dialogue asking one's way

A: Excuse me for troubling you sir, but can you tell me the way to the museum?

B: Certainly. Keep straight on along this road, take the first turn to the right, and that will take you to a green square with flagpoles. That is Istanbul Square; cross it, and you'll see a corner of a red-brick building with a couple of domes. That is the museum.

A: Thanks very much indeed.

B: My pleasure. (A goes on walking and takes the wrong turn. He wanders around a good deal. Tired and upset, he talks to a passer-by.)

A: Pardon me, sir, does this road lead to the museum?

B: I am sorry, sir. I don't know. I am a complete stranger here myself. (Another gentleman C on hearing this, stops.) Yes. Keep straight this way for over a mile and a half until you come to C: Chowk Azadi, then turn to the left. But it is a good way.

A: How far, do you think?

C: Over two miles, I should say. I'd take a bus, if I were you.

A: What number or route please?

C: Take number 117 when you come to Chowk Azadi. That will take you to the museum.

A: Thanks.

Dialogue between a brother and a sister concerning time

What is the time? Ali: Fatimah: It is nearly five minutes to eight by my watch. Upon my word, we must hurry up, if you are to catch that train to Rawalpindi.

Ali: Fatimah: Why, when is it due out? At quarter past nine exactly. Ali: Fatimah: Oh, never mind.

We have plenty of time. I am not so sure of that. What on earth have you been doing?

What time did you get up? Ali: Fatimah: I woke up before half-past five. Then I performed ablution and offered my morning salat.

Now breakfast is ready. Don't look at me like that. For Heaven's sake, get ready!

We have not a minute to lose. Time flies, you know. Ali:

Dialogue between a tailor and a customer

(Father is about to set up the tape-recorder, he calls aloud Yasser, Anne). Come over here. Hurry up! (They show up in a minute.)

Father: You are going to hear a dialogue on the tape now.

Yasser: Father! What is it about?

Father: Well, see this picture. (There is a picture of a tailor and a customer. Father switches on the tape-recorder. They listen with attention.)

Tailor: Good morning, Sir, what can I do for you?

Customer: I should like to be measured for a suit.

Tailor: With pleasure, Sir, kindly step this way. What style and shade would you prefer?

Customer: I want an ordinary lounge suit made of brown tweed. How much would the stitching cost?

Tailor: I could make you a suit for Rs. 2000/-. It is quite reasonable, sir.

Customer: That's right.

Tailor: Could you manage to call in sometime next week for the try?

Customer: Yes, just give me a ring. Here is my card.

Tailor: Very good, sir. Good morning. (Father takes out the plug and talks to his kids.)

Father: What do you say to that, kids?

Yasser: Very interesting, Dad.

Anne: Father I'll hear it again and then we will practise it. Yasser will act out as the tailor, and I shall be the customer.

lessons.title: Paragraph Specimens 1-4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A paragraph is about one topic only - begin with a topic sentence.
  • Give facts and details in order, then close with a finishing sentence.
  • Keep the paragraph short and clear - about 100 to 150 words.

My School

My school is a place of great charm for me. Although its building is pretty old, it seems to cast a spell on us. Some of the walls are massive and ceilings are very high.

Even the cruel summer fails to make our classrooms hot and humid. The location of my school is just by the side of the historic fort. The high walls of the fort, scarred with signs of wind and weather, look wonderful.

They have a mystery of their own. We understand our history lesson very well because of the nearness to the famous fort. The teaching staff at my school is kind and devoted.

A large playground with a row of evergreen tall trees faces the school building. What is more, it is away from all the hustle and bustle of the main road. I am glad that my school is far ahead of others in good results, sports, debates, library and scouting.

Girl Guides

Girl Guides is a British organisation of girls. It was founded by Baden Powell and his sister Lady Agnes in 1910. The main objective of this movement is to make teenage girls conscious of their responsibilities.

A member, a girl guide, is given a variety of programmes that shape her character. She learns, in association with other girl guides, how to keep herself clean and healthy. She is instructed how to build her moral and social character.

She learns the basic facts about courtesy and etiquette. Furthermore, a girl guide is taught how to develop home making abilities. She learns household skills like cooking, knitting, stitching, planning and maintenance.

A Visit to a Museum

The Lahore Museum is an important place where works of art and other objects of historical value are kept and displayed. It is an old imposing building with a high ceiling. The incharge of the museum is called the Curator.

Our well-informed teacher took us to different sections of the beautiful museum. There were neatly arranged glass-cases which displayed ancient swords, daggers, garments, ornaments, coins, bows and arrows. The items on display had tags with brief descriptions.

Paintings, pictures and clay models were exhibiting ancient craftsmanship. The huge statue of Queen Victoria was laid in one room of the museum. There were old manuscripts of the Holy Quran in another room.

Full-size doors and frames with primitive fittings were specimens of rare woodwork craftsmanship. The impressive display in the museum gave us a wealth of information and insight into our past. It was a rewarding visit indeed.

A River in Flood

Last summer, I was in my village, about twenty miles south of Jhang. For over a week, the wet spell had been a delightful experience. The rain was driven in sharp bursts by the rushing wind.

One morning, in the early hours there went up a cry "water! water!". The Chenab was in flood. There was water in our big courtyard.

The low-lying part of the village was under three feet of water. Panic gripped the whole village. There were bushels on almost every head.

Most of the folks started moving through the flooded fields towards the nearby high mound. It was a scene of great misery. From the corner of the high mound, I had the first glimpse of the river in flood.

The entire area upto the far-off road bridge and even beyond was just one sheet of muddy water. Logs were seen floating fast. The trees all around, with half of their trunks in water, stood firm like unfolded umbrellas.

Far below, we saw the floating horses and cows. The water all around and the floating objects in it filled our heart with dread.

lessons.title: Paragraph Specimens 5-8
lessons.notes_html:
A Pleasant Dream

Last night, I went to sleep a little early than my habitual time. I was exhausted so I fell slumbering immediately. In no time, I was in the land of dreams.

I dreamt that I have been selected for a scuba diving adventure with navy personnel. It was so exciting that I could feel butterflies in my stomach. Next, I found myself in the designated area where all the preparations took place.

I was given my body suit along with a mask, an oxygen tank and flippers. We all went to the boat. I was one of the trainees with navy officers.

They were pleasant but firm. The instructions were to be followed promptly. The boat took us to the middle of the ocean where the water was on a deeper side.

In reality, I did not know how to swim well, but in my dream, I could swim like a fish. On a count of three, we all dived in. To my surprise, I could see the underwater world really close.There were beautiful fish, corals and other sea creatures.

I was swimming between them effortlessly. The sun could be seen through the water, shining brightly in the sky. The leading officer soon instructed me to come out.

I followed the lead and got back to the boat. The head personnel was happy to see my stamina underwater. When he was about to shake hands with me, the alarm rang and I woke up for my morning prayers.

The feeling of freshness was so real that I could experience it even after waking up. It was a pleasant dream that made my day.

How to Keep Our Town Clean?

Cleanliness is next to godliness. We must give a serious thought to this golden truth. Neat and clean environment has a cheerful effect.

It is a sure sign of civilization. Knowledge is a great blessing of Allah. We are fortunate to have the opportunity to receive education.

As school going boys and girls, it is our responsibility to keep our town clean. We ought to develop civic sense. We should not throw fruit and vegetable peels all over the street.

A banana or melon peel thrown carelessly on the road may cause a fracture or even death. Plastic, polythene and wooden items should not be thrown into manholes. A choked gutter spreads filth and stench all over the street.

Life becomes miserable. Spitting is another problem as it causes disease and insanitation. We can politely prevent one another from spitting on floors.

We should not throw hard things or stones into toilets. We should not be shy of taking a broom and sweeping the littered portion of the street in front of our door. We should take care of trees, plants and flower-beds in parks.

If we happen to pass by an unattended running water tap, we should stop and close it. As citizens, we should be vigilant and should report to the municipality if its staff neglects its duty. We can also add to cleanliness if we sprinkle water on our portion of the road.

Dust and pollution can be effectively controlled if everyone lends a helping hand. Allah loves people who practise purity and cleanliness.

An Industrial Exhibition

An industrial exhibition was arranged in Islamabad in March last year. The intention of the organisers was to exhibit industrial products at one place. The trading community and the general public showed keen interest in the products.

Accompanied by my elder brother and sisters, I went around the elegant and brightly lit stalls. Exhibits included textiles and garments, electrical goods, household items, handicrafts, glass wares, furniture, sewing machines and stainless steel. The Pakistan Railways and WAPDA had put up informatory stalls.

Heavy industrial goods, rollers, water pumps, tube-well equipment, motors, fertilizers and machinery were also on display. Prices of consumer goods were quite reasonable. Manufacturers were selling their products at reduced rates.

Besides, there were food and entertainment stalls which attracted the cheerful crowd.

My Neighbour

Mr. Ashraf Minhas is my next door neighbour. He is a handsome, middle aged scholar with a vigorous zest for life. He is a real gentleman with a lot of goodwill.

You could not wish to meet a better natured and hospitable man. He likes gardening. His garden is full of flowers in spring.

He invites his neighbours and entertains them warmly. He delights everybody with fond details of lovely flowers and their blooming patterns. Mr. Minhas is an optimist by nature, that is why he never worries himself over trifles. He has a remarkable sense of humour, which helps him in getting along well with his neighbours.

He has a son and a daughter. They are known for their fine tastes and good manners.

lessons.title: Paragraph Specimens 9-11
lessons.notes_html:
Kitchen Gardening, A Hobby

People have different types of hobbies that they like to pursue in their leisure time. A healthy hobby keeps a person busy in a productive way. Also, it gives them pleasure and keeps them mentally healthy too.

Some of the hobbies include sewing, trekking, photography, painting, etc. My hobby is kitchen gardening. It keeps me in harmony with nature, plants, and other flora. I enjoy cultivating such fruits, vegetables. and herbs in my kitchen garden which I need everyday.

Kitchen gardening is not just gardening, it cultivates a lot of good habits in me such as eating healthy home grown fruits and vegetables, It also develops a great deal of patience in me, watching my plants every day, caring them for a long period, watering and pruning them. Kitchen gardening is a healthy hobby which keeps me active and give a sense of accomplishment when my family enjoy fresh organic vegetables, fruits and herbs.

Pakistani Women

Women in Pakistan have begun to take an active part in different spheres of life. Job opportunities for them in the past were few. By and large, women worked as lady doctors, nurses, health visitors and teachers during the first ten years of Pakistan.

But spheres for women now are greater than ever before. They seem well on the way to become even more active in the near future. They compete successfully in the Central Superior Services examinations.

They are holding responsible positions in administration, customs, income tax, railways, foreign services, police and postal departments. Some of them are in the assemblies as MNAs. Quite a number of educated women are in banks and businesses.

Pakistan had its first-ever woman Prime Minister in 1988 - 90 and again in 1994 - 1996. The women of Pakistan are now more conscious of their social and political status in the twenty-first century

Computers

Computers are a vital part of our daily lives. Let's look at how computers are used in numerous fields and why they are so essential. As a result of the computer's increasing importance and necessity in modern life, performing numerous tasks and activities has gotten simpler for us.

Computers can be used for a variety of tasks, such as swiftly and precisely solving mathematical equations, handling and processing data,storing information, and researching virtually any subject online. This remarkable invention was created in the second half of the twelfth century, and now it is essential to life. Calculators were invented in 1642 to make simple arithmetic operations like addition and subtraction easier.

With every good, there comes evil. People misuse computers and create trouble for other people and organisations. Such as; it is easy to invade someone's personal space.

Known people are easily distraught as their videos or information go viral on the internet. Without any investigation, people start spreading information which has a negative impact on that particular person's life. With great power comes great responsibility.

As much as computers liberate everyone and give access to the entire world, one has to be responsible. Students can easily use computers to conduct research, make an assignment, and take online classes and exams. Whereas, at offices, all of the data is stored in computers which saves paperwork and the environment s eco-friendly.
